description: We are Team AstraField, building a decision support tool for NASA’s Field Shift challenge that transforms open Earth data (POWER, MODIS, SMAP) into smart, climate resilient crop rotation plans to conserve soil and water. Our core team brings expertise in Python, Pandas, React.js, and GIS mapping.
summary:
TerraShift AI is a climate-smart agricultural decision-support platform developed by Team ASTRAFIELD for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms historical NASA POWER climate data into practical insights that help farmers explore how changing climate conditions and farm-specific factors can influence crop-rotation planning.

The platform analyzes historical temperature, rainfall, solar radiation, and estimated reference evapotranspiration, then combines these insights with user-reported farm information to compare five crop-planning strategies: current pattern, water-conscious, soil-health potential, climate-resilient, and balanced. Users can explore rainfall, temperature, and irrigation scenarios, review transparent calculations and assumptions, interact with a farm map and 3D visualization, and export analysis reports.

TerraShift AI aims to make Earth-observation data more accessible and understandable for agricultural planning, particularly in the Punjab and upper Indus region. It is a research and screening prototype, not a validated yield predictor or replacement for local agronomic expertise.
details:
TerraShift AI — Project Details

1. What the Project Does

TerraShift AI is an interactive, climate-smart agricultural decision-support platform developed by Team ASTRAFIELD for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, under the challenge Adapting Farms with NASA Data.

The project transforms historical NASA POWER climate data into understandable, farm-specific insights that can support agricultural planning. It helps users explore how historical temperature, rainfall, solar radiation, and estimated reference evapotranspiration relate to crop-rotation planning.

Users can create or select a farm profile, enter its location, reported area, soil information, irrigation availability, existing crops, and planning priorities. The platform retrieves historical NASA POWER data for the selected location and processes it into climate indicators, visualizations, and comparative planning insights.

2. How It Works

TerraShift AI follows a transparent data-to-decision workflow:

  1. Farm profiling: Users enter farm details, location, area, soil information, irrigation budget, crop history, and priorities.
  2. Earth-observation data retrieval: The backend retrieves historical daily climate data from NASA POWER, including temperature, precipitation, and solar radiation parameters.
  3. Climate analysis: The platform analyzes rainfall patterns, temperature conditions, variability, dry spells, and other relevant indicators. It also calculates an estimated reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) using the Hargreaves method.
  4. Crop-rotation comparison: The system evaluates five planning categories: Current Pattern, Water-Conscious, Soil-Health Potential, Climate-Resilient, and Balanced.
  5. Scenario simulation: Users can modify rainfall, temperature, irrigation availability, and water-budget assumptions to explore how different conditions affect the screening results.
  6. Decision support and reporting: Users can explore visualizations, receive context-grounded guidance, and export analysis snapshots as PDF, JSON, and CSV files.

3. Key Features

  • Historical NASA POWER climate-data integration.
  • Interactive farm profiles and geographic location selection.
  • Climate dashboards, charts, and daily-data exploration.
  • Five explainable crop-rotation planning categories.
  • Adjustable rainfall, temperature, and irrigation scenarios.
  • A deterministic, context-grounded agricultural advisor.
  • Interactive map and a 3D illustrative farm visualization.
  • Exportable PDF reports, JSON analysis, and daily CSV data.
  • Data provenance, source metadata, assumptions, and limitations displayed for transparency.

4. Benefits and Intended Impact

Agricultural planning is highly dependent on local environmental conditions, yet interpreting scientific climate datasets can be difficult for farmers and other agricultural stakeholders.

TerraShift AI aims to reduce this gap by making historical Earth-observation information easier to explore and understand. Its intended benefits include:

  • Making NASA climate information more accessible for agricultural planning.
  • Helping users compare alternative crop-rotation strategies.
  • Encouraging water-conscious and climate-aware planning discussions.
  • Supporting better understanding of historical rainfall and temperature conditions.
  • Making assumptions and analytical limitations visible instead of presenting unexplained recommendations.
  • Providing an educational and research platform for exploring the relationship between Earth data and agriculture.

The initial regional planning focus is Punjab and the upper Indus plain, with an illustrative Sialkot farm profile included in the application.

5. Technology and Tools Used

Frontend

  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Recharts for data visualization
  • Leaflet for interactive mapping
  • Three.js for the 3D farm visualization

Backend

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Pydantic
  • SQLite for persistent application data
  • Uvicorn for serving the application

Data and analytical methods

  • NASA POWER API for historical meteorological and solar data.
  • Hargreaves–Samani method for estimated reference evapotranspiration.
  • Rule-based and weighted heuristic screening for crop-rotation comparisons.
  • Scenario calculations for exploring alternative climate and irrigation assumptions.

Development and testing

  • Git and GitHub for source-code management.
  • Pytest for backend testing.
  • Playwright for browser-based testing.
  • Node.js and npm for frontend development and builds.

The application does not require an external AI-provider API key. Its agricultural advisor uses deterministic, context-grounded logic rather than claiming to be an external large language model.

6. Creativity and Innovation

The central creative idea behind TerraShift AI is connecting Earth-observation data with an interactive farm-level planning experience.

Instead of simply displaying climate charts, the platform connects historical climate information with farm profiles, crop-rotation comparisons, adjustable scenarios, explainable screening indicators, and downloadable reports.

Its combination of NASA POWER data, transparent agricultural heuristics, scenario exploration, geographic visualization, and an interactive 3D farm environment creates an accessible way to explore climate-informed agricultural planning.

The platform also distinguishes reported information, retrieved observations, calculated estimates, and heuristic indicators so users can better understand where information comes from and how it should be interpreted.

7. Factors Considered

During development, the team considered:

  • Historical climate variability and regional environmental conditions.
  • Farm location and the spatial resolution of NASA POWER datasets.
  • Rainfall availability and irrigation constraints.
  • Soil and crop information supplied by users.
  • Crop-family relationships and rotation-planning assumptions.
  • Transparency, traceability, and reproducibility of calculations.
  • Accessibility and usability for non-technical users.
  • The importance of communicating uncertainty and avoiding unsupported agricultural claims.

8. Limitations and Responsible Use

TerraShift AI is a research and screening prototype, not a scientifically validated crop-yield prediction system or a replacement for professional agronomic advice.

NASA POWER provides regional gridded historical estimates, not direct measurements from an individual farm. The ET₀ calculation, crop profiles, coefficients, crop calendars, and strategy scores require further local calibration and field validation.

The application does not guarantee crop yields, profitability, water savings, or successful agricultural outcomes. Its scenarios are explorations of assumptions, not future weather forecasts. Users should consult local farmers, agricultural experts, and extension services before making real-world decisions.

9. Future Development

Future work includes local agronomic validation, improved crop-calendar and soil calibration, field-based evaluation of water-balance assumptions, farmer usability studies, expanded regional applicability, and stronger privacy and deployment safeguards.

TerraShift AI — Intelligence for Every Field. Resilience for Every Harvest.

Developed by Team ASTRAFIELD for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
